tested_scope: One bounded official-GitHub documentation leaf on historical immutable-release tag reservation semantics across immutability disable/reenable, repository rename/transfer, reservation observability, and GitHub Free/no-finite-monthly-quota acceptance.

public_sources.observation: GitHub documents that after deleting an immutable release the associated tag may be deleted but the same tag name cannot be reused; it also documents non-reuse after deleting and recreating a repository with the same name.
GitHub documents that enabling release immutability applies only to future releases.
Current repository REST documentation exposes check/enable/disable immutable-releases state; retrieved documentation did not expose a historical reserved-tag identity/status endpoint.
Get-release-by-tag addresses an extant published release; it does not provide documented historical reservation status after the release is deleted.

GitHub Free public repositories are described as having a full feature set, but the bounded retrieved material did not explicitly bind immutable-release reservation semantics to a zero-finite-monthly-quota entitlement.

inference: The documented non-reuse rule is stronger than ordinary ref existence and survives repository deletion/recreation by name, so GitHub necessarily maintains some historical reservation state. However, the bounded official documentation retrieved here does not establish that this state survives an explicit disable/re-enable cycle, repository rename/transfer, or that callers can observe it through a reservation-specific API/error contract. Those missing semantics prevent using immutable-release tag reservation as a fully auditable Chat-native claim tombstone under the Phase-1 hard gates.

phase1_acceptance.minimal_unresolved_child: Determine whether immutable-release attestations or another official GitHub-owned artifact remain retrievable after release deletion and preserve immutable tag identity across repository rename/transfer; if not, the historical reservation remains non-observable for worker-side recovery.

conflict_check: Only own role-local LATEST and official public GitHub documentation were used after the mandatory presemantic witness. No O, other-role, downstream, legacy, shared-ledger, scheduler, or protected-primary semantic input/effect was used.
